solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Magnificent leading couples from Paris, lavish times always!

indicators.note: a leading couple is the front pair of letters, so each of the four following words gives its opening two letters

explanation.surface: A gushing tribute to a city of luxury, where the high life never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading couples from' takes the first two letters of each word: PA, LA, TI, AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatial describes something as grand as a palace, hence splendid or magnificent.

clue.text: Clever bishop? Correct

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
correct means right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bishop is clever and is told yes, that is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright person is quick-witted, a common synonym for clever.

clue.text: Talented following religion, not half trustworthy

indicators.note: the talent word comes after the religion fragment in the answer
taking only half of the word religion, its front four letters, leaves the rest behind

parts.note: talented means able

explanation.surface: A gifted believer whose faith is only half-hearted is described as dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the front half of the eight-letter word; 'following' sets the talent synonym after it, so 'religion' is not a definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reliable can be depended on, so the word is a synonym for trustworthy.

clue.text: Stick round a thoroughfare

indicators.note: the stick word goes round, enclosing the single letter

parts.note: a stick is a rod

explanation.surface: Someone plants a stick around a busy street, perhaps marking a route.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a public way for traffic, the everyday kind of thoroughfare.

clue.text: Coming from South, Noel tours a French church, getting meal

indicators.note: the reversed name travels around the French article and church, holding them inside
in a down clue, coming up from the south means the name is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Noel goes on a tour of a French church and is fed along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Coming from South' reads the name upwards, giving LEON; 'tours' wraps that round the French article and the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Luncheon is a formal word for lunch, the midday meal.

clue.text: Curt, put bar off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brusque command to a barman, telling him to close up the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges PUTBAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt reply is short and sharp, a synonym for curt.

clue.text: Boy welcoming English guide

indicators.note: the boy word welcomes, taking in, the single letter for English

parts.note: a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A young lad greets an English tour guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' puts E inside LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone is to show them the way, the verb sense of guide.

clue.text: Coiffure that's surprising at Irish party

parts.note: ha is an exclamation of surprise
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone's hairstyle at an Irish party causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's surprising' is not an anagram signal: it is the exclamation HA.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is a styled arrangement of hair, which is what coiffure means.

clue.text: Strange new Roman lab

indicators.note: new letters are made by rearranging the old ones into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An odd-looking new laboratory in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ROMANLAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means departing from the usual, so it is a synonym for strange.

clue.text: Featured in choir, perhaps, part of diocesan group

indicators.note: only part of the phrase diocesan group is taken, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Someone appeared in a church choir belonging to a diocesan group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' points to the letters across diocesAN Group.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sung is what a choir member does, so 'featured in choir' describes it, with 'perhaps' flagging the example.

clue.text: Skip journey

definitions.meaning: to skip is to ... along lightly
a short trip, especially a short flight

explanation.surface: A two-word note perhaps about missing out a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are ordinary senses: a little jump and a brief flight from one place to another.

clue.text: A cent tip? Outrageous!

indicators.note: something outrageous is wild and out of order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A customer is indignant at being tipped just one cent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outrageous' rearranges ACENTTIP; the whole clue also describes the answer, a tiny insulting sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small, inadequate amount of money, like a one-cent tip.

clue.text: Reportedly is familiar with disreputable bar — it will get you down fast!

definitions.text: it will get you down fast!

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: to be familiar with something is to know it, he knows
a dive is a seedy, disreputable bar

explanation.surface: Someone who knows a seedy bar well is warned it will drag them down quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' turns KNOWS into its sound-alike NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a steep, rapid plunge, as of an aircraft, so it brings you down quickly.

clue.text: Drink with king in wood

parts.note: tea is a drink
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king takes a drink out in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Teak is a hard timber from a tropical tree, a type of wood.

clue.text: A roadie at outset called Queen's musician

indicators.note: at the outset means the first letter of the word roadie is taken

parts.note: called on the phone means rang
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the abbreviation for the Queen; the 's is part of the surface

explanation.surface: A roadie tells how he was first to phone Queen's musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' is not the rock band but ER; 'at outset' takes R from roadie.
explanation.definitionFit: An arranger is a musician who adapts music for particular voices or instruments.

clue.text: Excitement as female friend returning

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the friend word is read backwards

parts.note: a friend is a pal

explanation.surface: There is a stir of excitement when a female friend comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns PAL into LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is a state of agitation or fuss, a mild kind of excitement.

clue.text: Dad's high point, becoming vicar

parts.note: Pa is a word for dad, so dad's gives pa's
a tor is a rocky hill or peak, a high point

explanation.surface: Dad's proudest moment came when he was ordained a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister in charge of a congregation, as a vicar is.

clue.text: Certain to accept surprisingly nice, attractive post

indicators.note: the certain word accepts, taking in, the rearranged letters

parts.note: certain means sure

indicators.note: surprisingly means in an unexpected way, so the letters of nice are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to take a pleasantly surprising, appealing job offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' gives INEC, and 'to accept' sets that inside the synonym for certain. 'attractive post' is one definition: a cushy job.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid position needing little work, so it is a desirable job.

clue.text: Coin word for policeman?

definitions.meaning: a ... is a low-value bronze or ... coin
a slang word for a police officer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a coin is the word for a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is both a British penny or two-penny coin and informal slang for a police officer.

clue.text: Era of silver finally gone

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so the last letter of gone is used

explanation.surface: A golden, or silver, age has come to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from gone.
explanation.definitionFit: An age is a distinct period of history, a synonym for era.

clue.text: Surf for missing Romeo, American

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the Romeo letter is taken out of for

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean surfer story: the waves are up but Romeo, an American, has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes R from FOR, leaving FO.
explanation.definitionFit: Surf is the white foam made by breaking waves, so the two words overlap.

clue.text: Cosy place, extremely nice, on street

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters, so nice gives its first and last

explanation.surface: An estate agent praises a snug home, very pleasant and right on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes NE from nice; 'on' in a down clue puts it above ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a snug, comfortable home, so it is used figuratively for a cosy place.

clue.text: Colour proposal — is not keen initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each of the four words gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone is lukewarm about a suggested paint colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of proposal, is, not, keen.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink is a pale red hue, one of the colours.

clue.text: No credit unfortunately for set of beliefs

indicators.note: things going wrong unfortunately mixes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A sad remark that someone's creed earns them no credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges NOCREDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a body of teachings held by a church or school of thought.

clue.text: Needleworker brings in cook's last item used to prepare food

indicators.note: the needleworker word brings in, holding inside, the letter from the cook

parts.note: a sewer is someone who sews, working with a needle

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the word cook

explanation.surface: A seamstress hands the chef the last kitchen tool needed for the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needleworker' is SEWER (one who sews), not a drain; 'cook's last' is K, which 'brings in' puts inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a long pin for holding meat or vegetables together while cooking.

clue.text: Newly independent guy has hesitation about me at first

indicators.note: the hesitation-and-me piece comes first, before the guy
the hesitation sound goes about, around, the word me

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation
taken as written
a guy is a gent

explanation.surface: A man stalls, umming about himself, as his nation gains freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the hesitation sound round 'me' to make EMER, and 'at first' puts that ahead of the guy.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergent is used of nations that have recently gained independence and are developing.
